title: Operator consent fastpath & change signet PRD (draft)
summary: Introduce a lightweight operator consent flow (Fastpath) and a compact signed change artifact called a 'Change Signet' to speed low-risk customer-managed network operations while preserving verifiable audit trails.
motivation: Customers frequently ask for faster small change windows during on-prem or VPC handoffs (DNS updates, route adds, NAT tweaks). Full evidence bundles are slow and increase onboarding friction. We need a middle lane: fast, low-cost, verifiable, and auditable for low-risk operator changes without compromising enterprise requirements.
success_criteria: Reduce median time-to-apply small network changes for pilot customers from 24h -> <2h
Generate a tamper-evident change artifact (Change Signet) for every Fastpath action stored in the audit index
Allow customer-side operator token-based fast approvals with KMS-backed signatures and enforce automatic rollback triggers when signet validation fails
Provide SLO for signet retention query latency (<200ms) in Console audit searches for 90% of queries
design_overview: Fastpath = a policy-controlled route that lets pre-approved operators submit limited-scope changes using a short-lived signed token. On submit, the control plane creates a Change Signet: compact JSON with change delta, fingerprint, operator signature (KMS/HSM), policy tag, risk score, and optional snapshot link. The signet is stored in the immutable audit index and is anchored by a hash chain to regular full evidence bundles. Heavy changes (routing table > X entries, firewall rules touching more than N subnets, or policy-elevated resources) are rejected from Fastpath and routed to normal full-attestation flow.
core_requirements: Policy DSL for administrators to declare which change types are Fastpath-eligible
Short-lived operator credentials (OAuth + customer-managed KMS signing) or delegated operator tokens
Change Signet schema v1 and validation library (open-source) for customers to verify locally
Immutable storage of signets with indexable fields (operator id, customer id, change type, timestamp, signet hash)
Immediate telemetry events emitted: signet_created, signet_validated, signet_rejected, signet_rollforward, signet_rollback
Console UX to search, filter, and replay signet context alongside full evidence when available
telemetry_and_audit: Each Fastpath action emits structured trace with request_id and signet_hash
Aggregate daily risk score distribution for Fastpath events exposed to customers (data exportable)
Retention default: 90 days for signets in pilot, configurable up to customer SLA (1y, 7y)
Cross-check job that runs hourly to validate signet chain integrity and flag gaps for operator review
Export format: NDJSON with canonical fields and optional base64 snapshot pointer
rollout_plan: Phase 0: internal lab tests (2 weeks) + signet schema freeze. Phase 1: pilot with 3 low-risk customers (6 weeks) — enable Fastpath by feature flag and collect telemetry. Phase 2: productize UX, add delegated KMS flows, and provide SDKs + validation library (8 weeks). Phase 3: gradual enable by customer size with audit SLAs and compliance review (ongoing).
open_questions: What is the precise threshold for 'low-risk' changes? Proposal: <5 route entries changed OR single-subnet firewall tweak
Do we require customer to store full evidence snapshots on their side or can we host ephemeral snapshots for X days?
How do we integrate with customer HSMs that disallow signing over external network? (suggested: local signing agent + attestable nonce exchange)
Policy DSL backward-compatibility with current approval gates — should we auto-translate existing gate rules or require manual migration?
Regulatory: does banking/legal require full evidence for any network change even if low-risk? Need compliance sign-off for pilot customers in regulated industries.
decisions_log: 2024-12-12: Chose Change Signet over minimal audit record because signet supports customer verification locally
2024-12-18: Fastpath scope limited to network config primitives; excluded PKI and key-rotation operations
2025-01-08: Default signet retention set to 90 days for pilot to limit storage costs
security_and_compliance_notes: Signets must be signed by KMS-backed keys controlled by operator or delegated admin. We will support customer-provided KMS (AWS KMS IAM role) and an on-prem signing agent for air-gapped installations. All signet metadata is treated as PII-adjacent and will be redaction-aware in exports. Compliance will need a mapping doc from signet fields -> evidence requirements for SOC2/GDPR/PCI customers.
ux_notes: Console will surface a 'Fastpath' toggle on operator profiles and a compact signet viewer with the signature validation state. Provide a one-click 'Request full evidence' that triggers snapshot bundling and attaches to the signet. Include an audit timeline view that shows signet -> evidence chain.
implementation_risks: Customers mistakenly configure overly permissive Fastpath policies
Signature verification differences across KMS vendors leading to false rejects
Storage cost growth if signets are retained by default for large fleets
Legal/regulatory rejection in high-compliance customers slowing adoption
